newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria, Russia, Greece may set up oil consortium.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria, Russia, Greece may set up oil consortium.

text.p: Bulgaria, Russia and Greece may set up a consortium for the construction of a planned oil route supplying Russian crude to the Balkans, local state news agency BTA said on Friday.
BTA said experts from the three countries had signed a protocol, designed to inform their governments over the establishment of "institutional structures, most probably a consortium."
Construction Ministry officials were not immediately available for comment.

Russia, Bulgaria and Greece plan a tanker route from the Russian Black Sea port of Novorossiisk to Bourgas in Bulgaria from where a new pipeline would carry Russian crude to Alexandroupolis in Greece.
A tripartite meeting at government level was delayed due to elections in Russia and Greece. Bulgaria has presidential elections on October 27.
Bulgarian deputy prime minister Doncho Konakchiev said last week the route was now being considered as a part of a greater regional project linking the Black Sea to a Caspian Sea oil pipeline.
